default.rules:
goal and status describe what someone is after and what they are doing now. Write them only when they changed in this reply, or for a person who is away from the scene. Never restate an unchanged one. When one has ended, write it as "clear" (goal: clear). Never write "Unknown".
Do not write who is present; the scene says. Write where: only for a named person who is somewhere other than the scene, and only when the reply tells you where (~ npc Name | where: the harbour office). Never write where for someone in the scene, and never "Unknown".
Do not write habits, tics, personality, speech style or how someone decides. They are written later from several scenes. The one exception is a change you can see in this reply: write ~ npc Name | look: what changed (clothes, a wound, a new form) as the full current look in one sentence. If the story states a person's gender, age or birthday outright, write it (gender: female) once.
New people: the first time a named person appears who is not in the list above, write + npc Name | role | look. role is two or three words (the harbour clerk). look is one short phrase of what you wrote about their appearance, at most 100 characters; leave it out for someone from the character card. That is all. Do not write their background, speech, mannerisms, secrets or anything else here; the full profile is filled in from the story afterwards. Never write + npc for a person already listed, and never for the player or the character you play. A title alone (the guard) is not a person until the story gives a name.
Write only what changed in this reply. Never write "keep", an empty value, a summary of the relationship, or a field again with the same value. Match people by the names in the list above; a person already listed with only a title who now has a name is the same person: use the listed name.
Memories: the words of a line you write (why:, a lie, a milestone) are saved as that person's memory. Do not write them again. Only for a moment no line covers (a confession, a promise, a shared joke) write ~ memory Name | what happened in one past-tense sentence. At most two a reply. Never repeat or reword a memory already stored.
Death: when the story shows that a named person died (not "almost", not a rumour, not a wound), write ~ npc Name | died | how: one sentence. This is final: never write that person as alive, present or speaking afterwards. Never write died for someone whose death you are unsure of.

event_watch.context: STORY EVENTS to look for (present NPCs' hidden notes): sec_0aaa1111 = Mira: The duke is exposed as a traitor | sec_0bbb2222 = Oren: the seal is shown. An event counts only when it happens as written, by the actor it names ("pressed" needs someone to press that person on it); the person raising the topic themselves, a mention, a hint or something about to happen does not. Because there is no JSON block in the reply, a secret event is written as a line: ~ reveal Name | opened: <key> | quote: "short exact quote from this reply". Only when the event happened as written, by the actor it names. No quote, no line.

metersParagraph.default: Relationships: when the scene changes how someone feels about {{user}}, write one line: ~ npc Name | trust: up | tension: down | impact: meaningful | why: what happened. Name each meter that moved (trust, affection, desire, tension) and say up or down; never write a number. impact is one word for the whole line: ordinary (a kind word, most moments) | meaningful (a real favour, a shared secret) | major (saved from danger, a betrayal) | extreme (a life-changing turning point, very rare). Leave impact out for ordinary. why is one short sentence naming the cause. Desire moves only for explicit attraction or intimacy. A continuation or aftermath of something already written is no change; write no line. Add | via: praise, gift, help, flirt, threat, shared-danger when the move is one of those approaches; the same approach to the same person again soon gives less, then backfires.
